issues.description: The full Europe results and Germany coverage preparation require the author-version Amadeus source histories and country-year section files, but the release excludes those materials. The cited historical product note does not establish a compatible substitute: compatibility must preserve static snapshots, historical financial items, ownership, harmonized firm IDs and industry mappings, and the 2016 WRDS contribution.

The separate German Destatis branch requires confidential URS_panel.dta and GWS_panel.dta inside the secure FDZ workflow. The documented author order is local Amadeus coverage (AMA_coverage) → FDZ URS/GWS cleaning and outcomes → Data merge using the passed local coverage → analyses → screened outputs returned; the field-level approved extract and local figure handoff remain to be resolved.

Europe Regulation.do imports MAD.csv and IFRS.csv and merges each by country. Europe Data.do later consumes ifrsdate (derives ifrs_year), tpdyear and madyear. The raw CSV rows/history and ownership of ifrsdate/madyear are unverified; no producer or source for tpdyear is identified. Preserve these known consumer names and key without assigning tpdyear or fields to a guessed source.

Counties.csv is readable and includes a raw header `ags (all)`, while AMA_panel.do later keeps/renames `agsall`. The exact Stata import-delimited normalization of this header was not checked; confirm the required field maps before treating the local coverage branch as closed.

SAS_Conversion_to_STATA.sas invokes conversion for 2018 at line 185, while the author documents a WRDS download from November 2016 and says the SAS-to-Stata conversion is used for 2016. The supported correction is to set the invocation to 2016 after preserving the supplied year-specific data path; no conversion was run.

The SAS WRDS macro supports section/year inputs but the current call requests Activities only; the downstream workflow also consumes Company/Amadeus, Financials, Auditors and Shareholders/Ownership. The source header specifies PC SAS Connect and WLATIN1; both SAS scripts enumerate Windows `dir` output via PIPE and parse the first ten characters as mmddyy10. The local SAS startup probe failed at TKELS, so section invocation, SAS/CONNECT, encoding and current Linux/UTF-8 host compatibility remain unverified. Do not invent a portable directory parser or infer entitlement from the startup error. The conversion macro derives lower-case country prefixes for output filenames, while Europe consumers form filenames from capitalized country labels; behavior on a case-sensitive host and the required simple staging/name mapping remain unverified.

evidence.description: The data and code description distinguishes the main Europe results from the confidential German supplement and the public-statistics supplement and describes the three project flows.
evidence.quote:
The main results of my paper are based on the Bureau van Dijk’s (BvD) Amadeus data (discs & WRDS
download). Those data are commercially available. The supplemental results in Section 7.2 on the
German enforcement reform are based on confidential data of the German Federal Statistical Office
(URS & GWS). Those data are accessible at the research data center of the statistical office (contingent
on acceptance of a research proposal and payment of access/data preparation fees). The supplemental
results in Section 7.3 on alternative productivity measures are based on National Statistics (KLEMS,
OECD, WIOD). Those data are publicly available.
The data and code are organized in four parts:
1. IGM-BvD Amadeus comprises the raw data (BvD Amadeus) and the relevant code (for
   downloading, cleaning, and converting the data).
2. Project Europe comprises the data and code for the main results using the BvD Amadeus data.
3. Project Germany comprises the data and code for the supplemental results in Section 7.2 using
   the data of the German Federal Statistical Office.
4. Project Statistics comprises the data and code for the supplemental results in Section 7.3 using
   the National Statistics data.
The code for the three projects (Europe, Germany, Statistics) is organized using the user-written
STATA command project (by Robert Picard). The command allows executing all STATA program
code of a given project in the relevant order. For more information, please refer to:

actions.description: Obtain/reuse the authorized Amadeus input route with distinct 2005–2015 disc snapshots and the separate 2016 WRDS contribution, or verify a compatible Orbis Historical route against the actual consumer requirements.
steps: Preserve static company and ownership snapshots for disc vintages 2005–2015, and financial history from the 2005, 2008 and 2012 discs as the author describes.

Preserve the separately supplied 2010 disc-vintage Bankers branch: run the included importer producer for country_Bankers_2010 with accnr and banker* fields, then validate the consumer’s accnr/b* field mapping. This is a 2010 Amadeus-disc path; do not add Bankers 2016 calls.
Retain the 2016 WRDS download as a separate input; include the company, financial, auditor and ownership/shareholder sections consumed in the supplied Europe and Germany paths.
Stage section files under the paths expected by the supplied importer and panel programs, preserving country, source vintage, identifiers, industry coding and fiscal-year history.

If using Orbis Historical, verify its country population, static snapshot semantics, financial items/history, ownership fields, identifier transitions, industry mapping and contribution for the 2016 branch; exact original bytes are not required when this compatibility is established.
validation: Compare acquired section names, fields, identifier and industry mappings, country coverage, vintage dates, and historical year coverage with the supplied Companies.do, Panel.do and AMA_data.do consumers before building panels.

validation: Confirm the file is tab-delimited with the expected oldid column and verify one-to-one/duplicate ID transitions before running Companies.do.

actions.description: Acquire the official candidate World Bank annual series only after checking their coverage against the author panel, then format them for the two supplied text-file consumers.
steps: Check the official PA.NUS.FCRF and NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS series for the exact required countries, Euro-area entry, 1999–2015 sample years and 2015 conversion/rebasing observation.

If coverage is compatible, export WB_nominal_exchange_rate.txt and WB_GDP_deflator.txt with tab-delimited countryname, time and value fields; preserve the code’s legacy currency mapping, exchange-rate normalization and within-country 2015 deflator rebasing.

validation: Confirm field names, annual country-year uniqueness, required 1999–2015 observations and 2015 base values; check the Euro-area and late-euro currency cases used by the supplied code.

review_notes: SAS/WRDS section and host contracts are explicit: current call is Activities only; required 2016 sections need calls through the supplied section/year macro. The author source requires PC SAS Connect/WLATIN1 and uses Windows `dir` PIPE output with first-ten-character date parsing; conversion emits lower-case country prefixes while Europe consumers form capitalized names. Linux/UTF-8 and filename-case compatibility remain unverified. The 2018→2016 source edit is conditional on staged 2016 inputs. The 2010 Bankers dependency is traced to the supplied importer producer and its Companies.do consumer; raw banker*/b* field mapping remains to verify. No author programs, estimators or simulations were executed; no SAS retry, restricted-data access, dataset download, package install or author-source mutation occurred. Bounded metadata inspection of supplied packaged data was performed: one-row table probes, streaming of the original OECD header/first record, and a read-only inspection of the WIOD DATA worksheet’s first two rows; no full analysis dataset was materialized.
